decision_conditions: The proposed development would provide a permanent new Class E catering van with seating area outside of a town centre and no sequential test has been provided which could undermine the vitality and viability of Enfield town centres, this would be contrary to Policy SD6 and SD7 of London Plan (2021), Policy CP17 and CP18 of the Core Strategy (2010) and Policies DMD25 and DMD32 of the Development Management Document (2014) and the National Planning Policy Framework

The proposal would represent inappropriate development, which is, by definition, harmful to the Metropolitan Open Land.  And in the absence of any very special circumstances to outweigh the visual harm to the Green Belt, contrary to Policy G2 of the London Plan (2021), Policies CP30 and CP33 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010),  Policy DMD82 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014) and the advice contained within the National Planning Policy Framework (in particular section 13).

The proposal by virtue of introducing an urbanised setting would result in the less than substantial harm to designated heritage assets and harm to non-designated heritage assets, in conflict with the objective of the framework with Chapter 16 of the NPPF, Core Strategy Policy 31 and Policy DMD 44 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The nature of the change of use would result in increased activity and general noise and disturbance which would be exacerbated by the proposed opening hours. The applicant fails to provide sufficient information to fully assess the impacts of noise potentially generated by the use on the amenities of nearby residential properties.  The proposed development, in the absence of an adequate noise report, fails to demonstrate appropriate measures to reduce adverse exposure to noise, contrary to Section 12 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), to policies D11, D13 and D14 of the London Plan (2021), to policies CP30 and CP32 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), and to policies DMD8, DM37  and DMD68 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The proposal would result in detrimental harm to trees protected by a Tree Preservation Order and others of significant quality, without sufficient justification or mitigation. As such, the development is contrary to Policies G6 and G7 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD37 and DMD80 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), and the guidance set out in the British Standard BS 5837:2012 - Trees in Relation to Design, Demolition and Construction.

The proposed development fails to provide any mechanism to secure the statutory Biodiversity Net Gain or demonstrate the required 10% uplift in biodiversity value, contrary to Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as inserted by the Environment Act 2021), Section 16 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP36 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD78 and DMD79 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).
